newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon government resigns, Hariri expected back.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon government resigns, Hariri expected back.

text.p: Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and his government resigned on Tuesday in the wake of recent parliamentary elections to allow the formation of a new cabinet which the billionaire tycoon is expected to head.

Hariri, in office since October 1992, is expected to come back stronger at the head of his third cabinet with the help of Syrian-backed supporters in parliament who won a crushing victory in the elections that ended September 15.
"The mandate of the council of ministers has ended according to the constitution so this government has resigned," Hariri said after a meeting with President Elias Hrawi.

Hariri and his 29-member cabinet will stay on in a caretaker capacity until the formation of the new government -- the third in four years headed by the 51-year-old politician who has launched a multi-billion dollar drive to rebuild Lebanon from the 1975-90 civil war.

Consultations to choose a new prime minister will begin when parliament elects a new speaker on October 22. Hrawi will hear the views of each of the 128 deputies and must name the majority choice to head the new government.
The elections, in which Hariri won his first parliamentary seat, confirmed the Sunni Moslem politician's position as one of Lebanon's most powerful political figures.
Unlike his two previous periods in office when he had virtually no allies in parliament, Hariri now heads one of the biggest blocs in the house after 20 of his supporters won seats.
The elections returned a predominently pro-Syrian legislature although they were marred by accusations of fraud, including vote-buying and illegal voting in the name of the dead people and emigrants.
Hariri's election victory is expected to make it easier for him to be reappointed and to push through projects in his ambitious reconstruction plan which were blocked by the previous parliament.
A visit to Lebanon by French President Jacques Chirac on October 24-25 will interrupt Hrawi's consultations on selecting a new prime minister.

However, official sources have said the formation of a new government, which must receive a parliamentary vote of confidence, would probably be completed by the end of this month or the start of November.
Hariri, whose personal fortune is estimated at $4 billion, has worked since coming to power to reestablish international confidence in Lebanon after the 1975-90 civil war.
His two previous governments strengthened the Lebanese pound which hit a record low of 2,750 to the dollar in 1992. It is now 1,557.25 to the dollar.

But critics say Hariri has plunged Lebanon deeply into debt with borrowings on the international capital markets to finance reconstruction. Total external and internal debt have soared to an unprecedented 16 trillion pounds ($10.3 billion).
Hariri, whose critics also say he has no social policy that takes into consideration the poor, said on Monday that the new government should make social policy a top priority.
